extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors and reviewers submitting to or reviewing for eLife
extracted.subtask_description: Official description of eLife's peer review and publication workflow (Reviewed Preprints, eLife Assessments, Public Reviews) including responsibilities, versioning, fees, and how assessments summarize significance and evidence. Intended to guide authors, reviewers and editors interacting with eLife.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewed Preprint publication model
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no accept or reject decision after peer review: rather, every article we review is published as a Reviewed Preprint. A Reviewed Preprint includes the preprint itself, the eLife Assessment, Public Reviews that describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and a response from the authors (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach emphasizes the scientific content of individual articles rather than journal name; Reviewed Preprints can be cited by their DOI and/or their eLife citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for peer review (editorial criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife editors — who are all active researchers — discuss new submissions and decide which will be peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific criteria used by editors are discussed in 'How and why eLife selects papers for peer review' (linked elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities: Public Review and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each peer reviewer is asked to write a Public Review of the article, and to recommend ways in which the authors could improve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Reviews are published as part of the Reviewed Preprint and should describe strengths and weaknesses and provide constructive recommendations for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment — significance of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife Assessments summarise the significance of the findings reported in an article using a common vocabulary on a scale ranging from 'landmark' to 'useful'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor and the peer reviewers write an eLife Assessment that summarises the significance of the findings; the Assessment is published alongside the Reviewed Preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment — strength of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife Assessments summarise the strength of the evidence in an article using a common vocabulary on a scale ranging from 'exceptional' to 'inadequate'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assessment should reflect how strongly the data support the claims; editors and reviewers consult when writing Assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Reviews — justification of claims and explicit disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Reviews describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data. Where the reviewers disagree with the claims in an article, this is made explicit within the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must make clear whether conclusions are supported; explicit disagreements among reviewers/editors are recorded rather than hidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations published with Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to the authors for improving the article are published as part of the Version of Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors publish a Version of Record (VOR) these recommendations remain part of the public record; revised versions will include updated Assessments and Public Reviews as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning and updates policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review and publishing process has stages: Publication of Reviewed Preprint, publication of a revised version (with updated eLife Assessment and Public Reviews), and (optionally) publication of a Version of Record to mark the end of review and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are free to submit revised versions; version two of the Reviewed Preprint will include the revised preprint, updated Assessment and Public Reviews, and an author response if available. At any point following peer review authors can choose to publish a VOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint availability policy
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife works with authors to make all submissions selected for peer review available as preprints. Authors may submit to eLife directly or transfer a preprint from bioRxiv or medRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing in eLife combines the advantages of preprints with the scrutiny offered by peer review; this policy promotes speed and openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access / funder compliance and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of an eLife Version of Record (VOR) complies with all major funding agency requirements for immediate online access to the published results of their research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VORs are typically indexed by services such as Google Scholar, PubMed, PubMed Central, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, and DOAJ, but inclusion is subject to each indexing service's own criteria and cannot be guaranteed. An increasing number of funders are recognising Reviewed Preprints in research assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our publication fee is $3000 and is payable at the peer review stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee is waived for anyone who cannot afford to pay; payment is requested at the peer review stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation among editors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers consult with each other during the peer-review process, especially when writing eLife Assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation aims to produce coherent Assessments and to ensure that disagreements are explicitly recorded where they exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limit on number of articles reviewed or published
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not artificially limit the number of articles it reviews or publishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects a policy choice to avoid restricting publication based on arbitrary quotas; selection is based on editorial criteria rather than fixed caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation policy for Reviewed Preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewed Preprints can be cited by their DOI and/or their eLife citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making expert evaluations part of the published paper aims to improve research assessment and evaluation practices.
